title: Fetal growth restriction and multiple pregnancy
blurb: Risk-assess and monitor fetal growth with Saving Babies' Lives v3 element 2, act on a small baby, and understand chorionicity, scan schedules and timing of birth for twins and triplets (NICE NG137).
question: At 34 weeks, Esi's symphysis fundal height plots below the 10th centile on her customised chart. She has been on the low-risk pathway. What should the midwife do?

teach.h: Small for gestational age and growth restriction
teach.body: A small for gestational age (SGA) baby has an estimated fetal weight (EFW) below the 10th centile. Fetal growth restriction (FGR) means the baby has not reached its growth potential. Formally (SBL v3.2, appendix C), FGR in the current pregnancy is an EFW or abdominal circumference below the 3rd centile, or below the 10th centile with evidence of placental dysfunction (abnormal uterine or umbilical artery Doppler). In plain English: small is a size; FGR is a small baby who is struggling. A slowing growth trend also matters, even above the 10th centile.
teach.cite: NHS England SBL v3.2 element 2 and appendix C

teach.h: SBL v3.2 element 2: the growth pathway

steps.label: FGR risk assessment by 14 weeks
steps.sub: Include previous birthweight centiles; digital BP

steps.label: Low risk: SFH
steps.sub: From 24+0, first by 28+6, no more than 2-weekly

steps.label: Increased risk: growth scans
steps.sub: Every 3-4 weeks until birth; SFH stops

teach.caption: SBL v3.2 2.1-2.13. Risk is reviewed throughout pregnancy, and women move between pathways as risk changes.

rows.label: Growth check
values: Serial SFH, plotted on a chart

teach.caption: SFH measurement stops once serial scan surveillance begins (SBL v3.2 2.12). NG201: offer a growth scan if SFH is small.

teach.body: Assess fetal wellbeing, including a discussion about fetal movements and, if needed, a computerised CTG. Assess the woman at each contact: BP with a validated digital monitor and urine for proteinuria; follow NICE on PlGF testing if she is hypertensive. Before 34+0 weeks, umbilical artery Doppler is the main surveillance tool, at least every 2 weeks, with fetal medicine network input. Discuss and agree every decision about timing of birth with her.

teach.h: Timing of birth for a small baby (SBL v3.2)
head: Finding (no other risk factors)
Timing of birth
rows: Initiate at 37+0, no later than 37+6 weeks
teach.caption: SBL v3.2 2.18-2.20. Reduced fetal movements, abnormal Doppler, cCTG not meeting criteria, hypertension or reduced liquor prompt earlier review.

teach.h: Twins: chorionicity drives the risk (NICE NG137)

root.label: Twin pregnancy on scan
root.sub: Determine chorionicity when twins are detected

children.label: Growth scans from 24 wks
children.sub: Every 28 days or less; birth at 37 weeks

teach.caption: Chorionicity uses the number of placental masses, membranes and the lambda or T-sign. If it is unclear, manage as monochorionic until proven otherwise (1.1.7).

items.label: EFW discordance: increase to at least weekly scans with Doppler
discordance plus one baby under 10th centile: refer to tertiary centre
planned birth for uncomplicated trichorionic or dichorionic triamniotic triplets
twin cervix or less: vaginal progesterone 200 mg nightly

teach.caption: No routine cerclage, Arabin pessary or bed rest to prevent preterm birth in twins (1.5.6). Multiple pregnancy is a moderate risk factor for pre-eclampsia; aspirin if 2 or more risk factors (1.6.2).

items: Esi's SFH plots below the 10th centile. The midwife explains the finding and arranges an ultrasound growth scan (NG201 1.2.32).
She asks about fetal movements and reminds Esi to report any reduction straight away.
She checks BP with a validated digital monitor and tests urine for protein.
The scan shows EFW on the 6th centile with normal Dopplers. Esi moves to the scan pathway; SFH stops.
Birth is considered at 39+0 and achieved by 39+6 weeks unless other risk factors appear; decisions are agreed with Esi.

teach.text: Below the 3rd centile and between the 3rd and 10th centile have DIFFERENT timings: 37+0 to 37+6 versus considering 39+0 and achieving by 39+6. And for twins, it is CHORIONICITY (shared placenta), not zygosity (identical or not), that sets the risk.

items: SGA: EFW below 10th centile. FGR: below 3rd centile, or below 10th with placental dysfunction.
Risk-assess for FGR by 14 weeks; high risk: uterine artery Doppler 18+0-23+6; increased risk: scans every 3-4 weeks.
Low risk: SFH from 24+0 (first by 28+6), plotted; stop SFH once serial scans start.
EFW below 3rd: birth 37+0-37+6. 3rd-10th: consider 39+0, achieve by 39+6.
Twins: DCDA 37 weeks, MCDA 36, MCMA 32+0-33+6; MC twins scanned every 14 days from 16 weeks for TTTS.

summary: You can now place women on the right fetal growth pathway, measure and act on SFH, recognise SGA and FGR, and apply SBL v3.2 timing of birth. You can also explain chorionicity and the NG137 scan schedules and planned birth dates for twins and triplets.

A.q: A low-risk woman is having routine antenatal care. According to SBL v3.2, when should serial symphysis fundal height measurement start?
A.why: SBL v3.2 2.10: low-risk women have SFH measured at each appointment after 24+0 weeks (no more often than 2-weekly), with the first by 28+6 weeks.

whyNot.0: SFH is not started at 16 weeks; the uterus is still small and measurements are not used then.
whyNot.1: SBL v3.2 starts serial SFH after 24+0, not 20+0.
whyNot.3: Starting at 28 weeks is later than SBL v3.2 advises; the first measurement should be by 28+6.

A.q: A woman at high risk of FGR is booked into maternity care. Between which gestations should she have uterine artery Doppler assessment?
A.why: SBL v3.2 2.7: women at high risk of FGR should have uterine artery Doppler between 18+0 and 23+6 weeks.

whyNot.0: 11+2 to 14+1 weeks is the dating and combined screening window.
whyNot.2: This is later than the SBL v3.2 uterine artery Doppler window.
whyNot.3: This is when serial growth scanning often begins, not uterine artery Doppler.

A.q: A twin pregnancy is seen at the 12-week scan but chorionicity cannot be determined, even after referral. How should the pregnancy be managed?
options: As dichorionic until a later scan
A.why: NG137 1.1.7: if it is difficult to determine chorionicity, manage the pregnancy as monochorionic until proven otherwise.

whyNot.1: Assuming dichorionicity would under-monitor a pregnancy that may share a placenta.
whyNot.2: A twin pregnancy is never managed as a singleton.
whyNot.3: The default is monochorionic, not monoamniotic, which needs separate evidence.

B.q: A growth scan at 36 weeks shows an EFW below the 3rd centile with no other risk factors. What does SBL v3.2 recommend about timing of birth?
B.why: SBL v3.2 2.18: EFW below 3rd centile with no other risk factors: initiate labour or birth at 37+0 and no later than 37+6 weeks.

whyNot.0: Considering birth at 39+0 applies to EFW between the 3rd and 10th centile.
whyNot.2: Waiting to 41 weeks exposes a growth-restricted baby to increased stillbirth risk.
whyNot.3: There is no indication here for immediate caesarean; timing is 37+0 to 37+6.

B.q: A woman with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy asks how often she will be scanned to look for feto-fetal transfusion syndrome. What does NICE advise?
B.why: NG137: monitor for feto-fetal transfusion syndrome with ultrasound every 14 days from 16 weeks until birth in monochorionic pregnancies.

whyNot.0: Every 28 days from 24 weeks is the maximum interval for dichorionic twin growth scans.
whyNot.1: First-trimester screening for TTTS is not offered, and weekly scans are for specific concerns.
whyNot.3: This interval and start point do not match NG137.

B.q: A woman with an uncomplicated dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy asks when birth will be planned. What does NICE NG137 advise?
B.why: NG137 1.9.9: offer planned birth at 37 weeks for uncomplicated DCDA twins.

whyNot.0: 36 weeks is for uncomplicated monochorionic diamniotic twins.
whyNot.1: 38 weeks is later than NG137 advises for DCDA twins.
whyNot.2: 32+0 to 33+6 is for uncomplicated monochorionic monoamniotic twins.

C.q: Ruth is on the low-risk pathway. At 33 weeks her SFH has plotted on the 50th, 40th and now the 15th centile, crossing centiles downward. What should the midwife do?
C.why: A slowing growth velocity (a downward trend in centiles) indicates increased risk and needs review, even above the 10th centile (SBL v3.2 appendix C); a growth scan is arranged.

whyNot.0: Waiting 4 weeks would delay identifying a baby whose growth is slowing.
whyNot.2: Declining growth velocity matters even when the measurement is above the 10th centile.
whyNot.3: Induction is not decided on SFH alone; a scan and review come first.

C.q: A woman with dichorionic twins has a scan showing an EFW discordance of 22%, both babies above the 10th centile. What change does NG137 recommend?
options: At least weekly scans with UA Doppler
C.why: NG137: increase monitoring to at least weekly with umbilical artery Doppler for each baby if EFW discordance is 20% or more and/or any EFW is below the 10th centile.

whyNot.0: Discordance of 20% or more needs more frequent monitoring than 4-weekly.
whyNot.1: Discordance alone does not indicate immediate birth.
whyNot.2: Laser therapy is a treatment for feto-fetal transfusion syndrome in monochorionic twins.

C.q: Grace's baby has an EFW on the 7th centile at 37 weeks with normal Dopplers, normal liquor and normal movements. When should birth be planned?
C.why: SBL v3.2 2.19: EFW between the 3rd and 10th centile: consider birth at 39+0 and achieve it by 39+6, unless other risk factors are present.

whyNot.1: Birth at 37+0 to 37+6 applies to EFW below the 3rd centile.
whyNot.2: Waiting to 42 weeks ignores the recommended 39+6 limit for an SGA baby.
whyNot.3: Birth before 39 weeks needs other risk factors, which are absent here.

reteach.title: Size, trend and placenta
reteach.question: Three questions decide how worried to be about a baby's growth: how small, which way is it heading, and is the placenta working?

blocks.body: How small: below the 10th centile is SGA; below the 3rd is FGR on size alone. Which way: a baby crossing centiles downwards is at risk even above the 10th. Placenta: abnormal uterine or umbilical artery Doppler turns a small baby into a growth-restricted one. The answers decide the scan plan and the timing of birth, always agreed with the woman.

blocks.h: EFW centile and SBL v3.2 action

blocks.text: Monochorionic twins share a placenta: that is why they are scanned every 2 weeks from 16 weeks and born earlier (36 weeks) than dichorionic twins (37 weeks).

explain.body: Assess aspirin need at booking; complete an FGR risk assessment by 14 weeks, including previous birthweight centiles; record BP with a validated digital monitor; review risk throughout pregnancy (SBL v3.2 2.1-2.8).

items.label: Uterine artery Doppler if high risk

test.q: By what gestation should the FGR risk assessment be completed under SBL v3.2?
test.why: SBL v3.2 2.4: perform a risk assessment for FGR by 14 weeks' gestation.

whyNot.0: 10 weeks is the booking target, not the FGR risk assessment deadline.
whyNot.2: 20 weeks is the anomaly scan; risk assessment should already be done.
whyNot.3: 24 weeks is when SFH begins; the risk assessment is needed much earlier.

explain.body: Low risk: SFH at each appointment after 24+0 (first by 28+6), plotted on a chart. Increased risk: growth scans every 3-4 weeks until birth; SFH stops once scans begin. FGR before 34+0: umbilical artery Doppler at least every 2 weeks with fetal medicine input.

test.q: A woman on 3-4 weekly growth scans asks why her midwife no longer measures her bump. What is the correct explanation?
options: SFH stops once serial scans start
SFH is not useful after 32 weeks
SFH is done by the sonographer
test.why: SBL v3.2 2.12: women having planned serial scan surveillance should cease SFH measurement once serial surveillance begins.

whyNot.1: SFH continues to term for low-risk women; it stops because scans replace it.
whyNot.2: Her BMI is not the reason given; the scan pathway is.
whyNot.3: Sonographers measure fetal biometry, not SFH.

explain.body: EFW below the 3rd centile: initiate at 37+0, no later than 37+6. 3rd to below 10th: consider at 39+0, achieve by 39+6. Declining growth velocity meeting criteria: plan from 37+0. All decisions discussed and agreed with the woman.

test.q: Who should agree decisions about the timing of birth for a baby with suspected FGR?
options: The woman, with the clinical team
test.why: SBL v3.2 2.18: all management decisions about timing of birth for FGR babies should be discussed and agreed with the mother.

whyNot.0: The sonographer provides measurements but does not decide timing of birth.
whyNot.1: The obstetrician advises, but the decision is discussed and agreed with the woman.
whyNot.3: The neonatal team may be consulted, but the decision is agreed with the woman.

explain.body: Determine chorionicity when twins are detected (placental masses, membranes, lambda or T-sign); unclear means monochorionic. MC twins: TTTS scans every 14 days from 16 weeks. DC twins: growth scans from 24 weeks at no more than 28-day intervals. Planned birth: DCDA 37, MCDA 36, MCMA 32+0-33+6, uncomplicated triplets 35.

test.q: Which ultrasound sign helps identify a dichorionic twin pregnancy in the first trimester?
test.why: NG137 1.1.3: chorionicity is determined by the number of placental masses, the amniotic membranes and the lambda or T-sign; the lambda sign indicates dichorionicity.

whyNot.1: The double bubble sign suggests duodenal atresia.
whyNot.2: The lemon sign is a skull shape linked with spina bifida.
whyNot.3: The banana sign is a cerebellar shape linked with spina bifida.
